rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 is the best design so far (score 211.8). Raising kd from 0.6 to 0.9 with speed 1.1, kp 4.5 and ki 0.3 unchanged gave 5 oval completions out of 20, s-bend progress of 0.36, and oval progress of 0.75. Every track still ends at max_error of about 0.059 to 0.064 m, which is the off-track limit, so the robot overshoots the tape on bends rather than drifting slowly. Slalom is the weakest track at 0.07 progress, with almost no line loss, which points to a slow steering response on alternating bends. Line-loss events are near zero, so the 16 mm sensors at ±0.06 m are adequate and I keep them. Oval oscillation is 0.31, so there is little margin to raise kd again. Iteration 6 H2 said that if max_error stays at the limit, steering authority is the constraint. Turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more yaw rate per unit of PWM differential. Change: wheel_track 0.14 to 0.11 m, the only change, so the effect on overshoot and slalom can be read cleanly. Controller stays at base 1.1, kp 4.5, ki 0.3, kd 0.9. Expected result: effective steering gain rises by about 27 percent, max_error falls below 0.06 on some bends, slalom progress rises above 0.15, and oval completions hold or increase. Risk: higher effective gain could increase oscillation above 0.4 on oval. Hypotheses for next race: (H1) if oscillation rises above 0.4 with no gain in max_error, the extra authority is the problem and kp should fall back to about 4.0. (H2) if max_error is unchanged at about 0.06 on the same bend, speed is the limit and base_speed should drop to about 1.0 while kd stays at 0.9. (H3) if all tracks survive but do not finish, base_speed should rise to about 1.2. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
